# Assembly Guide

How to build an OpenFlaps display, in three parts:

1. **[Assemble one character](#part-1--assemble-one-character)** — steps 1–10
2. **[Daisy chain of four characters](#part-2--daisy-chain-of-four-characters)** — steps 11–13
3. **[First character with the Pico case](#part-3--first-character-with-the-pico-case)** — step 14

Print the parts first — see [PRINT-GUIDE.md](PRINT-GUIDE.md).

> **Status: Part 1 confirmed against a real build.** Its order, hardware and wire
> routing follow an actual character assembled by hand; each step shows photos of that
> build next to the CAD figure.
> Parts 2 and 3 show photos of a real build too; Part 3's order and cabling follow it.
> Anything marked ⚠️ is inferred from the CAD, or missing from it, and worth checking
> against a real build.

## Orientation

All figures use the same convention as the CAD:

- **Front** — the open window you read the flaps through.
- **+X** — the side with the gears and the Lid. Characters are joined along X, and the
  Pico case goes on the +X end.
- The wheel axle and the motor shaft both run along X.
- One character is **34.5 mm wide** (its pitch along X).

# Part 1 — Assemble one character

![Exploded character](images/02-exploded-character.png)

| # | Part | # | Part |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frame | 8 | 28BYJ-48 stepper motor |
| 2 | Left Wheel | 9 | Stepper Motor Gear Spacer |
| 3 | Flaps (only 2 shown here; see note below) | 10 | Gear 50x30 – Stepper 30 |
| 4 | Limit Switch Support | 11 | Character PCB |
| 5 | Micro limit switch | 12 | Lid |
| 6 | Right Wheel | 13 | Front Connector Pegs (4) |
| 7 | Gear 50x30 – Wheel 50 | | |

> **Note:** from here on, every figure shows only the two flaps the CAD model itself carries,
> to keep the pictures readable — the wheel is actually loaded with all 45, pegged all
> the way around. Step 5 shows the fully loaded wheel.

## Step 1 — Print the flaps

Follow *Printing the character flaps* in [PRINT-GUIDE.md](PRINT-GUIDE.md). You need
45 flaps per character, in the order of `char_set` in the ATtiny84 firmware:

```
 ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789.,:-!?/°
```

The Left Wheel has exactly 45 peg holes on its flange (one per flap). Before you
hang any flaps, dry-fit the wheel parts and mesh the two gears; sand stiff gear teeth
lightly with 400-grit paper.

## Step 2 — Prepare the limit switch

The micro limit switch needs its cable attached before it goes anywhere near the wheel —
there's no way to solder it once it's inside the drum.

1. Cut off the switch's middle pin.
2. Solder a two-conductor wire (about 20 cm) to the two remaining, outer pins.

**From a real build:**

| As it comes | Middle pin cut, wires soldered |
|---|---|
| ![As it comes](images/photos/01a-limit-switch-before.jpg) | ![Middle pin cut, wires soldered](images/photos/01b-limit-switch-wired.jpg) |

## Step 3 — Mount the switch in its holder

![Limit switch](images/04-limit-switch.png)

1. Drop the two **M2 thin nuts (4)** into the hex pockets on the far (−X) face of the
   **Limit Switch Support (1)**.
2. Set the **micro limit switch (2)** on the flat of the hub, lever pointing outwards,
   and push the two **M2×12 screws (3)** through it from the +X side. Tighten.
3. Route the switch's wire out through the opening in the middle of the Limit Switch
   Support.

The switch is triggered once per wheel revolution and gives the module its home
position.

**From a real build:**

| Parts | Switch screwed on | Wire through the middle |
|---|---|---|
| ![Parts](images/photos/02a-switch-holder-parts.jpg) | ![Switch screwed on](images/photos/02b-switch-screwed-to-holder.jpg) | ![Wire through the middle](images/photos/02c-wire-routed-through-holder.jpg) |

## Step 4 — Assemble the wheel

![Wheel](images/05-wheel.png)

1. Drop the two **M2 nuts (2)** into the pockets in the drum wall of the
   **Left Wheel (1)**, from the open end.
2. Slide the **Limit Switch Support with its switch (3)** into the open end of the drum,
   wire first. It is wider than the hole in the flange, so it can only enter from this
   end; its shaft points out along +X.
3. Put the **Right Wheel (4)** on the open end, over the Limit Switch Support's shaft, and
   start the two **M2×8 screws (5)** into the nuts. Leave them **a bit loose**
   for now — you'll tighten them once the flaps are in, in the next step.

**From a real build:**

| Parts | Holder in the Left Wheel | Right Wheel on, screws loose |
|---|---|---|
| ![Parts](images/photos/03a-wheel-parts.jpg) | ![Holder in the Left Wheel](images/photos/03b-switch-holder-in-left-wheel.jpg) | ![Right Wheel on, screws loose](images/photos/03e-wheels-joined-back-screwed.jpg) |

## Step 5 — Insert the flaps

![Flaps and gear](images/05b-flaps-gear.png)

1. Insert the **flaps (1)**: each has a peg at each end. The Right Wheel has a small raised
   tab next to one peg hole; that hole takes the flap printed with `°` on one face and a
   space on the other. Push the pegs into the holes on the Left Wheel flange and the
   Right Wheel starting there, all 45 around, as shown fully loaded here. (The
   **Wheel 50 gear (2)** shown alongside isn't pressed on yet — that's step 8.)
2. Tighten the two wheel screws from step 4.

The drum should now spin freely on the Limit Switch Support.

**From a real build:**

| The tab on the Right Wheel | Loading the flaps | All 45 in |
|---|---|---|
| ![The tab on the Right Wheel](images/photos/04c-alignment-peg-closeup.jpg) | ![Loading the flaps](images/photos/04d-flaps-partially-loaded-side.jpg) | ![All 45 in](images/photos/04f-flaps-fully-loaded-top.jpg) |

## Step 6 — Install the wheel in the Frame

![Frame](images/06-frame.png)

Feed the switch's wire through the small hole at the base of the Frame's axle post, so
it comes out on the back (−X) face, then lower the **wheel assembly (2)** onto the axle
from the +X side, so the axle post seats in the Limit Switch Support. The flaps face the
open front window. On the back face, lay the wire in the diagonal slot molded into it, and
push it back into the case through the small hole at the end of the slot.

**From a real build:**

| Wire through the axle hole | Wire in the diagonal slot at the back | Wheel on the axle, wire back inside |
|---|---|---|
| ![Wire through the axle hole](images/photos/05b-wire-through-axle-hole.jpg) | ![Wire in the diagonal slot at the back](images/photos/05d-frame-back-wire-exit.jpg) | ![Wheel on the axle, wire back inside](images/photos/05e-wheel-in-frame-wire-routed-back.jpg) |

## Step 7 — Install the motor

![Motor nuts](images/06b-frame-nuts.png)

1. From the outside (−X side), drop the two **M3 nuts (1)** into the hex pockets in the
   Frame's −X wall.

![Motor](images/06c-motor.png)

2. Slide the bare **motor (1)** — no gear or spacer on it yet — into the Frame from the
   +X side, shaft towards you, so its two ears lie against the inside of the −X wall
   over the nuts.
3. Secure the motor's two ears with the two **M3×20 screws (2)** into the nuts.

**From a real build:**

| Parts | Motor screwed in |
|---|---|
| ![Parts](images/photos/06a-motor-and-screws-parts.jpg) | ![Motor screwed in](images/photos/06b-motor-mounted-in-frame.jpg) |

## Step 8 — Gear up the motor to the wheel

![Drive train](images/03-drive-train.png)

1. Slide the **Gear Spacer (2)** onto the **motor (1)** shaft, down to the motor face.
2. Press the **Wheel 50 gear** onto the hex boss of the Right Wheel.
3. Press the **Stepper 30 gear (3)** onto the motor shaft, over the spacer, meshing it
   with the Wheel 50 gear. Its D-shaped hole matches the flat on the 28BYJ-48 shaft, so
   it only fits one way.

The spacer is 4 mm and lifts the small gear clear of the motor body so it lines up with
the 50-tooth gear on the wheel; the axes are 40 mm apart
(15 + 25 mm pitch radii).

**From a real build:**

| Spacer on the shaft | Wheel 50 on the wheel | Stepper 30 meshed |
|---|---|---|
| ![Spacer on the shaft](images/photos/07b-spacer-on-stepper-shaft-closeup.jpg) | ![Wheel 50 on the wheel](images/photos/07c-big-gear-on-wheel.jpg) | ![Stepper 30 meshed](images/photos/07d-gears-meshed-closeup.jpg) |

## Step 9 — Wire up the Character PCB

![Character PCB](images/07-pcb.png)

1. Flash the ATtiny84 firmware on the **Character PCB (1)** first, through its 6-pin ICSP header,
   following [INSTALL-attiny84.md](../firmware/attiny84/INSTALL-attiny84.md). Do it now, before the
   board goes into the Frame.
2. Cut the switch's cable to length, then crimp a 2x1 2.54 mm header onto its two ends.

![Switch cable](images/08-cable.png)

3. Plug the **micro limit switch (2)**'s connector and the **motor (1)**'s five-wire plug
   into the **Character PCB (1)**'s headers.
4. Slide the PCB into the pocket at the top of the Frame. Run both cables, the motor's
   and the switch's, under the bar next to the motor and up along the side wall to the
   PCB, so they stay clear of the gears.

> The switch's cable itself isn't a modeled CAD body yet, so the figures above show only
> its two connector ends — see step 6 for how the wire is actually routed from the
> switch, through the Frame, to here.

Before closing the Lid, turn the wheel by hand and check that the limit switch clicks
once per revolution. Its position matters: too early or too late makes `home`
miscalibrate.

**From a real build:**

| Crimped switch connector | Both plugged in | Cables under the bar, PCB in place |
|---|---|---|
| ![Crimped switch connector](images/photos/08c-crimped-switch-connector-closeup.jpg) | ![Both plugged in](images/photos/08d-pcb-connected-closeup.jpg) | ![Cables under the bar, PCB in place](images/photos/08e-pcb-installed-in-case.jpg) |

## Step 10 — Lid and Front Connector Pegs

![Corner nuts](images/09a-corner-nuts.png)

1. Make sure the Character PCB is fully seated and sits flush in its pocket.
2. Turn the Frame round and drop the four **M3 nuts (1)** into the hex
   channels at its corners, from the back (−X) face. They sit deep in the channels.

![Lid and connectors](images/09-lid-connectors.png)

3. Press the **Lid (1)** onto the +X face. It covers the gears, holds the PCB with its
   curved hood (this replaces the old PCB Holder), and has a hole for the wheel shaft.
4. Put a **Front Connector Peg (2)** on each of the four corners of the Lid, and fasten each
   with an **M3×20 screw (3)** through it, all the way into the nut at the back.

> The character that will sit next to the Pico case (Part 3) gets **no Front Connector Pegs**,
> and its corner nuts stay empty: the Pico case is fixed to it directly.

The Front Connector Pegs stand out from the +X face: they plug into the matching hex
pockets on the −X face of the next character, or of the Pico case.

| Front | Back |
|---|---|
| ![Front](images/10a-character-front.png) | ![Back](images/10b-character-back.png) |

**From a real build:**

| Parts | Front Connector Peg over a screw | Closed up |
|---|---|---|
| ![Parts](images/photos/09a-lid-and-fastener-parts.jpg) | ![Front Connector Peg over a screw](images/photos/09c-peg-on-screw-closeup.jpg) | ![Closed up](images/photos/09e-closed-case-front-question-mark.jpg) |

**One character is done.** Repeat steps 2–10 for every character.

# Part 2 — Daisy chain of four characters

Build four characters (Part 1), then join them. The first character, the one that will
take the Pico case (Part 3), is built **without** Front Connector Pegs and corner screws in step 10.

![One character's wheel](images/11-chain-wheel.png)

Each character going into the chain already has its wheel loaded (Step 5) and closed up
(Steps 6–10) — a reminder, with only 2 of the 45 **flaps (1)** shown, as elsewhere in this
guide. There's no way to add flaps once the wheel is inside the Frame, so this has to be
done before joining the characters, not after.

## Step 11 — Join the characters

![Joining four characters](images/12-chain-join.png)

1. Line the characters up along X, with the first one at the +X end. Push the four **Front
   Connector Pegs (1)** of each character into the hex pockets on the −X face of the character
   in front of it, until the Frames butt together at a 34.5 mm pitch.
2. Repeat until all four are joined.

**From a real build** (a generic block of four, so the end character keeps its
pegs; the block next to the Pico case leaves them off, see Part 3):

| One character | Two joined | Three joined | All four |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![One character](images/photos/10a-chain-one-character.jpg) | ![Two joined](images/photos/10b-chain-two-joined.jpg) | ![Three joined](images/photos/10c-chain-three-joined.jpg) | ![All four](images/photos/10d-chain-four-joined.jpg) |

## Step 12 — Character Attachment Clips

![Character Attachment Clips](images/13-chain-clips.png)

Clip a **Character Attachment Clip (1)** across the top edge of each joint and one across
the bottom edge **(2)**, so each pair of neighbouring Frames is held in line. Three joints
take six clips. The Frames have matching grooves on their top and bottom edges; the clip
is symmetric, so either way round fits, with its hooked ends pointing into the groove.

## Step 13 — Backboard PCB

![Backboard PCB](images/14-chain-backboard.png)

Lay the **Backboard PCB (1)** into the channel across the backs of the four Frames, with
the **UP ↑** arrow printed on it pointing to the top of the display. It has one connector
per character and gives the chain power (the 5V connector) and the I²C bus.

**From a real build:**

| Backboard PCB in place |
|---|
| ![Backboard PCB in place](images/photos/10e-chain-backboard.jpg) |

**The finished chain:**

| Front | Back |
|---|---|
| ![Front](images/15a-chain-front.png) | ![Back](images/15b-chain-back.png) |

The address of each character is assigned from the Pico afterwards (long-press the
module button, see CLAUDE.md, *Physical Button*).

# Part 3 — First character with the Pico case

The Pico case goes on the **first character of the chain** (the +X end), which has no Front
Connector Pegs: the case is screwed straight onto its Frame corners instead.

![The character's wheel, again](images/16-pico-wheel.png)

The same reminder as Part 2: this character's wheel is already closed up with all 45 flaps
in place (only 2 **flaps (1)** shown). The Pico case goes on the outside of the Frame and
doesn't touch the wheel.

## Step 14 — Pico case

![Pico case](images/17-pico-case.png)

1. Drop the four **M3 nuts (3)** into the standoffs of the **Pico Case (1)** (they sit inside, out of sight in the figure), set the **Pico PCB (4)**
   on them with the Pico W in its sockets, and fasten it with the four
   **M3×8 screws (5)**.

**From a real build:**

| Parts | Pico PCB screwed in |
|---|---|
| ![Parts](images/photos/11a-pico-case-parts.jpg) | ![Pico PCB screwed in](images/photos/11b-pico-pcb-in-case.jpg) |

2. Set the case on the Lid of the first character and fasten it at the four corners with the
   **M3×20 screws (2)**, from inside the case, into the corner nuts in the Frame.

**From a real build:**

| Case and first character | Case on the first character | On the block of four |
|---|---|---|
| ![Case and first character](images/photos/11c-case-and-first-character.jpg) | ![Case on the first character](images/photos/11e-case-on-first-character.jpg) | ![On the block of four](images/photos/11f-case-on-block-of-four.jpg) |

3. Connect the Pico PCB to the Backboard PCB at the back of the display with two cables:
   - **power:** a 2-wire cable with **JST XH** connectors, from one of the Pico PCB's 5V
     outputs to the Backboard's **5V** connector;
   - **I²C:** a 2-wire cable with **2.54 mm pitch** connectors, from the Pico PCB's I²C header
     to the Backboard's **I2CIN** header.

**From a real build:**

| Power and I²C cables to the Backboard |
|---|
| ![Power and I²C cables to the Backboard](images/photos/11g-cables-to-backboard.jpg) |

4. Drop the three **M3 nuts (6)** into the slots in the top, bottom and front walls of the case, put
   on the **Pico Case Lid (7)**, with the "Open Flaps" lettering facing out, and fasten it
   with the three **M3×20 screws (8)**.

**From a real build:**

| Lid, screws and nuts | Lid on |
|---|---|
| ![Lid, screws and nuts](images/photos/11h-lid-parts.jpg) | ![Lid on](images/photos/11i-lid-closed.jpg) |

## Then

1. Deploy the Pico firmware (`firmware/pico/deploy.sh`).
2. Pair each character and calibrate its offset from the *Modules* page.

## Tips

- Sand gear teeth lightly if they bind (400-grit).
- If flaps don't clip on easily, check your extrusion multiplier; PLA shrinkage varies.
